title: Conditionals: elegí la forma correcta
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta. Primero decidí el tipo: ¿siempre verdadero, posible, hipotético o imaginario del pasado?

items.q: If a program ___ an invalid input, it usually returns an error message.
items.e: 'usually' → hecho general → Zero: If + Present Simple, Present Simple.

will receive: Zero Conditional (hecho general): If + presente, presente. will no va acá.
received: pasado simple sería Second Conditional (hipotético). La frase habla de un hecho general (usually): receives.
would receive: would sería Second Conditional (hipotético); acá es un hecho general: presente simple.

items.q: If the development team finishes the tests today, they ___ the new version tomorrow.
items.e: Situación posible en el futuro → First: will + base.

deploy: para una posibilidad futura (First Conditional) la cláusula principal lleva will: will deploy.
would deploy: would sería Second Conditional, pero la cláusula if está en presente (finishes): First → will deploy.
would have deployed: would have + participio es Third Conditional (pasado irreal). Acá la condición es futura: will deploy.

items.q: If I ___ more experience with Python, I would apply for that position.
items.e: Hipotético en el presente → Second: If + Past Simple.

have: la principal dice would apply → Second Conditional: If + pasado simple (had).
would have: would nunca va en la cláusula if: If I had.
had had: had had (past perfect) sería Third Conditional; con would apply es Second: If I had.

items.q: If we had backed up the database, we ___ all that data.
items.e: If + Past Perfect → Third: would have + participio.

wouldn't lose: la cláusula if tiene past perfect (had backed up) → Third Conditional: wouldn't have lost.
won't lose: won't sería First Conditional; con had backed up es Third: wouldn't have lost.
didn't lose: el Third Conditional lleva would have + participio en la principal, no el pasado simple.

items.q: If the server ___ down, users cannot access the application.

will go: Zero Conditional (hecho general): If + presente, presente. will no va acá.
went: pasado simple sería Second Conditional (hipotético). users cannot access es un hecho general: goes.
would go: would sería Second Conditional; acá es un hecho general: presente simple.

items.q: If I were the project manager, I ___ the deadline.
items.e: If I were → Second: would + base (no will).

will change: If I were... es Second Conditional: la principal lleva would, no will.
changed: el Second Conditional lleva would + verbo base en la principal, no el pasado simple.
would have changed: would have + participio es Third Conditional (pasado). If I were... es Second: would change.

items.q: If they had tested the application properly, they ___ so many bugs after the release.

wouldn't find: la cláusula if tiene past perfect (had tested) → Third Conditional: wouldn't have found.
won't find: won't sería First Conditional; con had tested es Third: wouldn't have found.
hadn't found: la principal del Third Conditional lleva would have + participio, no had.

items.q: If the client ___ the design, we will start development next week.
items.e: First Conditional: el if-clause va en Present Simple, nunca will.

will approve: en First Conditional la cláusula if va en presente simple, no con will: If the client approves.
approved: pasado simple sería Second Conditional; con will start es First: presente simple.
would approve: would nunca va en la cláusula if; con will start es First: approves.

items.q: If developers don't use version control, they often ___ track of changes.

will lose: Zero Conditional (hecho general): If + presente, presente. will no va acá.
would lose: would sería Second Conditional (hipotético); acá es un hecho general (often): presente simple.
lost: pasado simple sería Second Conditional. Acá es un hecho general (often): presente simple.

items.q: If I ___ the lottery, I would travel a lot.
items.e: Poco probable → Second: If + Past Simple (won). Se traduce 'si ganara'.

win: If + presente sería First Conditional; con would travel es Second: pasado simple (won).
had won: had won (past perfect) sería Third Conditional; con would travel es Second: won.
would win: would nunca va en la cláusula if: If I won.

title: Conditionals: escribí la forma del verbo
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. If the code contains a syntax error, the compiler usually [1] (display) an error message.
2. If we finish the testing phase this week, we [2] (release) the application next Monday.
3. If I were more familiar with JavaScript, I [3] (understand) this code more easily.
4. If we [4] (know) about the server problem earlier, we would have been able to fix it before the presentation.
5. If I had had more time yesterday, I [5] (write) better documentation.
6. If it [6] (rain) tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
7. If I [7] (win) the lottery, I would travel a lot.
8. If you [8] (heat) ice, it melts.
9. If you had studied, you [9] (pass) the exam.
10. If she [10] (be) here, she would help us.

pat: Zero Conditional (hecho general): presente en las dos cláusulas. will no va acá.
the compiler es 3.ª persona singular: displays (con -s).
items.e: Zero: Present Simple en ambas partes; the compiler → displays.

pat: la cláusula if está en presente (finish) → First Conditional: will release.
en First Conditional la principal lleva will: will release.
If I were... es Second Conditional: would understand, no will.
el Second Conditional lleva would + verbo base en la principal, no el pasado simple.
items.e: If I were → Second: would + base.

pat: would have been able (principal) indica Third Conditional: hace falta past perfect en if: had known.
would have nunca va en la cláusula if: If we had known.
el participio de write es written (write → wrote → written): would have written.
If I had had (past perfect) → Third Conditional: would have written.
items.e: Third: would have + participio (write → wrote → written).

pat: will no va en la cláusula if: If it rains.
would nunca va en la cláusula if: If I won.
con would travel (Second Conditional) la cláusula if lleva pasado simple: won.
items.e: Second: If + Past Simple, no would.

pat: Zero Conditional (hecho general): presente en las dos cláusulas. will no va acá.
con you el verbo no lleva -s: heat.
items.e: Verdad general: If you heat ice, it melts.

pat: If you had studied (past perfect) → Third Conditional: would have passed.
después de would have va el participio: passed.
items.e: If you had studied → would have passed.

pat: la principal dice would help → Second Conditional: pasado simple (were/was). is sería First; would no va en la cláusula if.
items.e: Second: If she were here (forma habitual de to be).

items.q: If the database connection fails, the application displays an error.

First Conditional: First = If + presente simple, will + verbo (posible en el futuro). Esta oración tiene presente + presente.
Second Conditional: Second = If + pasado simple, would + verbo (hipotético en el presente). Esta oración tiene presente + presente.
Third Conditional: Third = If + past perfect, would have + participio (irreal en el pasado). Esta oración tiene presente + presente.

items.q: If the client approves the design, we will start development next week.

Zero Conditional: Zero = If + presente simple, presente simple (hechos que siempre pasan). Esta oración tiene presente + will.
Second Conditional: Second = If + pasado simple, would + verbo (hipotético en el presente). Esta oración tiene presente + will.
Third Conditional: Third = If + past perfect, would have + participio (irreal en el pasado). Esta oración tiene presente + will.

items.q: If I were the project manager, I would change the deadline.

Zero Conditional: Zero = If + presente simple, presente simple (hechos que siempre pasan). Esta oración tiene pasado (were) + would.
First Conditional: First = If + presente simple, will + verbo (posible en el futuro). Esta oración tiene pasado (were) + would.
Third Conditional: Third = If + past perfect, would have + participio (irreal en el pasado). Esta oración tiene pasado (were) + would.

items.q: If they had tested the application properly, they wouldn't have found so many bugs after the release.

Zero Conditional: Zero = If + presente simple, presente simple (hechos que siempre pasan). Esta oración tiene past perfect + would have.
First Conditional: First = If + presente simple, will + verbo (posible en el futuro). Esta oración tiene past perfect + would have.
Second Conditional: Second = If + pasado simple, would + verbo (hipotético en el presente). Esta oración tiene past perfect + would have.

items.q: If developers don't use version control, they often lose track of changes.

First Conditional: First = If + presente simple, will + verbo (posible en el futuro). Esta oración tiene presente + presente (hecho general).
Second Conditional: Second = If + pasado simple, would + verbo (hipotético en el presente). Esta oración tiene presente + presente (hecho general).
Third Conditional: Third = If + past perfect, would have + participio (irreal en el pasado). Esta oración tiene presente + presente (hecho general).

items.q: If it rains, we'll cancel the trip.

Zero Conditional: Zero = If + presente simple, presente simple (hechos que siempre pasan). Esta oración tiene presente + will.
Second Conditional: Second = If + pasado simple, would + verbo (hipotético en el presente). Esta oración tiene presente + will.
Third Conditional: Third = If + past perfect, would have + participio (irreal en el pasado). Esta oración tiene presente + will.

items.q: If I won the lottery, I would travel a lot.

Zero Conditional: Zero = If + presente simple, presente simple (hechos que siempre pasan). Esta oración tiene pasado + would.
First Conditional: First = If + presente simple, will + verbo (posible en el futuro). Esta oración tiene pasado + would.
Third Conditional: Third = If + past perfect, would have + participio (irreal en el pasado). Esta oración tiene pasado + would.

items.q: If I hadn't been sick, I would have gone to your party.

Zero Conditional: Zero = If + presente simple, presente simple (hechos que siempre pasan). Esta oración tiene past perfect + would have.
First Conditional: First = If + presente simple, will + verbo (posible en el futuro). Esta oración tiene past perfect + would have.
Second Conditional: Second = If + pasado simple, would + verbo (hipotético en el presente). Esta oración tiene past perfect + would have.

items.q: If you heat ice, it melts.

First Conditional: First = If + presente simple, will + verbo (posible en el futuro). Esta oración tiene presente + presente (hecho general).
Second Conditional: Second = If + pasado simple, would + verbo (hipotético en el presente). Esta oración tiene presente + presente (hecho general).
Third Conditional: Third = If + past perfect, would have + participio (irreal en el pasado). Esta oración tiene presente + presente (hecho general).

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If it will rain, we'll cancel the trip.
If it rains, we'll cancel the trip.
If it rain, we'll cancel the trip.
items.a: If it rains, we'll cancel the trip.

will no va en la cláusula if: If it rains.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If I would win the lottery, I would travel.
If I won the lottery, I would travel.
If I win the lottery, I would travel.
items.a: If I won the lottery, I would travel.
items.e: Second: if-clause en Past Simple, no would.

If I would win the lottery, I would trav: would nunca va en la cláusula if: If I won.
mezcla First (win) con Second (would). Second Conditional: If I won..., I would travel.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If you studied, you would have passed.
If you had studied, you would have passed.
If you would have studied, you would have passed.
items.a: If you had studied, you would have passed.

mezcla pasado simple con would have. Third Conditional: If you had studied..., you would have passed.
If you would have studied, you would hav: would have nunca va en la cláusula if: If you had studied.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If I had more money, I will travel.
If I had more money, I would travel.
If I had more money, I would to travel.
items.a: If I had more money, I would travel.
items.e: Second: resultado con would, no will.

mezcla Second (had) con will (First). Second Conditional: I would travel.
después de would va el verbo base, sin to: I would travel.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If the tests will pass, we'll deploy.
If the tests pass, we'll deploy.
If the tests passed, we'll deploy.
items.a: If the tests pass, we'll deploy.

will no va en la cláusula if: If the tests pass.
mezcla pasado simple (Second) con will (First). First Conditional: If the tests pass, we'll deploy.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If we tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
If we had tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
If we would have tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
items.a: If we had tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
items.e: Third: had + participio en el if-clause.

If we tested the code, we wouldn't have: mezcla pasado simple con wouldn't have. Third Conditional: If we had tested...
If we would have tested the code, we wou: would have nunca va en la cláusula if: If we had tested.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If she were here, she would help us.
If she would be here, she would help us.
If she is here, she would help us.
items.a: If she were here, she would help us.
items.e: Second: If + were/Past Simple, would + base.

would nunca va en la cláusula if: If she were here.
mezcla presente (First) con would (Second). Second Conditional: If she were here.

title: Third Conditional con modales (might / could have)
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta. would have = seguro; might/could have = posible.

items.q: If it had snowed, it ___ terrible traffic problems.
items.e: Tu apunte: If it had snowed, it might have caused...

would cause: If it had snowed (past perfect) → Third Conditional: might have caused (con modal might).
might cause: might cause es Second; con had snowed es Third: might have caused.
might had caused: después de might va have + participio, no had: might have caused.

items.q: If she had studied more, she ___ a better grade.

could get: If she had studied (past perfect) → Third Conditional: could have gotten.
can have gotten: can no se usa así en un hipotético pasado; el modal pasado es could have.
could had gotten: después de could va have + participio, no had: could have gotten.

items.q: If you had been paying attention, you ___ the red traffic light.
items.e: Forma continua en el if-clause + would have + participio (see → saw → seen).

would see: If you had been paying (past perfect) → Third Conditional: would have seen.
would have saw: el participio de see es seen (see → saw → seen): would have seen.
had seen: la principal del Third Conditional lleva would have + participio; had seen va en la cláusula if.

items.q: The result is 100% certain: if we had practised more, we ___ won the match.
items.e: would have = certeza; might/could have = solo posible.

might have: gramatical, pero might expresa posibilidad. El ejercicio dice que el resultado es 100% seguro: would have.
could have: gramatical, pero could have expresa posibilidad/capacidad. El ejercicio dice que el resultado es 100% seguro: would have.
should have: should have expresa un reproche o lo que convenía hacer, no un resultado seguro: would have.

items.q: If it ___ snowed, the roads would have been closed.

has: has snowed es Present Perfect; el Third Conditional necesita past perfect: had snowed.
would have: would have nunca va en la cláusula if: If it had snowed.
did: did snowed no existe; el Third Conditional lleva had + participio.

items.q: If the team ___ the bug earlier, the release could have been on time.
items.e: Pasado imaginario → Past Perfect en el if-clause.

found: pasado simple sería Second; con could have been es Third: had found.
would find: would no va en la cláusula if; Third Conditional: If the team had found.
has found: has found es Present Perfect; el Third Conditional necesita past perfect: had found.

title: Del español al inglés: si pasa / si pasara / si hubiera pasado
instructions: Traducí mentalmente y completá. Recordá: el subjuntivo español ('si ganara', 'si hubieras estudiado') se dice con Past Simple / Past Perfect en inglés.
text:
1. Si ganara la lotería, viajaría mucho: If I [1] (win) the lottery, I [2] (travel) a lot.
2. Si estudiaras, aprobarías el examen: If you [3] (study), you [4] (pass) the exam.
3. Si hubieras estudiado, habrías aprobado: If you [5] (study), you [6] (pass) the exam.
4. Si hubiera testeado el código, no habríamos hecho deploy de ese bug: If we [7] (test) the code, we [8] (not / deploy) that bug.
5. Si los tests pasan, hacemos el deploy: If the tests [9] (pass), we [10] (deploy).

pat: en Second Conditional la cláusula if lleva pasado simple (won); ni would ni el presente van acá.
had won sería Third Conditional (pasado irreal). 'Si ganara' es Second: pasado simple.
Second Conditional: la principal lleva would, no will.
would have + participio es Third. 'Viajaría' (hipotético presente) es Second: would travel.
would nunca va en la cláusula if: If you studied.
had studied sería Third Conditional. 'Si estudiaras' es Second: pasado simple.
would have + participio es Third. 'Aprobarías' es Second: would pass.
will es First Conditional. Con la cláusula if en pasado simple (Second) la principal lleva would.
'Si hubieras estudiado' es Third Conditional: hace falta past perfect (had studied).
would have nunca va en la cláusula if: had studied.
'habrías aprobado' es Third Conditional: would have passed.
después de would have va el participio: passed.
'Si hubiera testeado' es Third Conditional: hace falta past perfect (had tested).
'no habríamos hecho deploy' es Third Conditional: wouldn't have deployed.
después de wouldn't have va el participio: deployed.
items.e: 'no habríamos hecho deploy' → wouldn't have + participio.

pat: will no va en la cláusula if: If the tests pass.
pasado simple sería Second; 'si los tests pasan' es First: presente simple (pass).
la cláusula if está en presente (pass) → First Conditional: will deploy.
en First Conditional la principal lleva will: will deploy.
